title: Registration data can be linked across contexts via stable identifiers
description: The registration flow includes strong identifiers such as email address and government ID. description: The parent registration flow contains directly identifying and highly sensitive personal data, including name, email address, government ID, and a six-digit code. Exposure of this flow content to unauthorized parties or internal overexposure at the Authentication Service would identify the parent and reveal more data than necessary for simple authentication.
assumptions: The flow or receiving process may be observable by unauthorized parties, logged excessively, or accessible to personnel/components without need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Specific node id is approximate; the applicability of identifiability is strong given the explicit identifiers in the flow.

description: If the Authentication Service does not create trustworthy records of the registration transaction, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate what data was submitted, whether the account was created by them, or what notices/consents were presented at registration. This undermines privacy accountability and dispute resolution.

description: Because the flow contains sensitive identity attributes, the parent may not understand why each field is requested, whether the government ID and six-digit code are mandatory, how long the data will be retained, or whether it will be shared for verification or fraud-prevention purposes. This creates an unawareness risk at registration.

uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; the threat clearly concerns insufficient transparency at collection time.
